text:
Maria: Quick idea — we can shave a bunch of NCCL/multi-GPU temp alloc overhead by aggregating per-shard comm/temp buffers into a single per-GPU slab and leasing slices out. Posting profiling + a tiny PoC.
Kyle: Sketch? Are we talking one big page-locked buffer per GPU that we slice for each TP shard/op?
Maria: Yep. Current observed pattern: each TP shard (and some kernels) create short-lived NCCL staging or temp tensors (~64–256MB) per request. Multiply by TP size and concurrent requests and we blow out memory. On 8-way TP test we see ~1.1–1.4GB extra from duplicated per-shard comm bufs.
James: That matches the nightly profile heatmaps I saw (nccl_tmp_allocs spikes). Can you paste before/after numbers from your PoC run?
Maria: PoC numbers:
- baseline (per-shard): peak GPU mem 12.4GB, comm+temp ~2.7GB
- slab allocation (shared per-GPU): peak 11.2GB, comm+temp ~1.5GB
- delta: ~1.2GB freed per GPU on 8-way TP. Latency impact: +0.3ms p95 on synthetic decode, throughput unchanged.
Lenore: Very promising. What's the exact allocator change? Pool-backed slab or bump-pointer ring? Any concurrency hazards with overlapping NCCL kernels?
Maria: Implementation notes: single page-locked slab per GPU, atomic bump allocator for quick reservations, plus a small free-list for large slices. We record a CUDA event on NCCL launch and return the slice only after the event is recorded + completed. That prevents reuse while ops are in-flight.
Pseudocode:
```
struct Slab { void* base; size_t size; atomic<size_t> head; }
reserve(size_t n) {
  off = atomic_fetch_add(&slab.head, align(n));
  if (off + n <= slab.size) return slab.base + off;
  // fallback: allocate fallback temporary (rare)
}
free_with_event(void* ptr, cudaEvent_t e) {
  // enqueue into retire queue and free when event completes
}
```
SRE-bot: Reminder: keep a fallback path for non-pinned allocations and single-GPU/low-memory cases. Also add a flag to toggle slab for debugging.
Anika: A couple of questions: (1) How does this play with our batching heuristics / continuous batching? If a shared slab gets occupied by long NCCL ops, could it cause later requests to stall waiting for a slice? (2) Will KV cache prefix reuse reduce demand anyway?
Kyle: Good call. We can add a reservation policy: smaller/short-lived slices for fine-grained ops, and a reserved pool for large contiguous staging buffers. Also expose `--nccl-comm-slab-size` and `--nccl-comm-alloc-mode={shared|per_shard}` for experiments.
James: Tests we need before merge:
- unit test for race-free retire queue (simulate overlapping events)
- memtoolkit integration to measure peak in 2/4/8 TP configs
- nightly perf job with seq_len=2048, batch=1..4 and concurrent N=16/32
Lenore: I'll run synthetic workloads tonight (seq 2048, batch 4, TP=8) and a stress with concurrent requests N=32. Will post logs. If the +/- mem numbers hold we should be able to enable this as an opt-in flag on Dedicated first.
Maria: Branch: git://redwood/repo#nccl-slab-poc (poC only). Requesting review from @Lenore @James @Kyle. Plan: ship as alpha toggle, enable for specific GPU SKUs where page-locked slab helps most.
Anika: Also add a perf guard to reject if p95 latency regresses by >1% and a memory regression detector in Optimize so we can recommend slab when it helps unit economics.
infra-bot: Deploy note: when toggling on in Dedicated, ensure we set `cudaHostAlloc` limits and monitor `nvml` OOM counts during rollout.
Kyle: Nice work. If the PoC is stable I'll follow up with a variant that shares staging buffer across models on the same GPU (cross-model slab) — could reduce memory further for bursty multi-tenant nodes.
Maria: Thanks — will iterate after Lenore's stress runs. :thumbsup:
